review_note: Which PowerFactory classes the typed Case can represent. The class census from the source dump is checked against this file: a class that is present in the source and absent here blocks the conversion by name and count. That is the point -- it makes 'we never taught CEPT about this class' a visible blocker instead of a silently different network. Moving a class into 'represented' is a claim that the typed Case carries its behaviour, not merely its name.

ElmLod.note: General load, ZIP/voltage-dependent where the source discloses it.

StaCubic.note: Connection point; carried as element terminal bindings.

TypLne.note: Line type; its parameters are read into the line row (r/x/c, rated current) rather than kept as a separate object.

TypTr2.note: Two-winding transformer type; parameters are read into the transformer row.

TypSym.note: Synchronous machine type; parameters are read into the generator row. The source-faithful dynamic lane additionally copies the native TypSym object rather than rebuilding it from these scalars.

TypSwitch.note: Switch type; rating parameters are read into the switch row.

TypLod.note: General load type. Verified against the 39-bus source: the ZIP/exponential coefficients (aP/bP/cP, aQ/bQ/cQ, kpu/kqu, kpf/kqf) are read into the load row, so voltage-dependent behaviour is carried rather than defaulted.

ElmShnt.note: Shunt capacitor or reactor. PowerFactory's shtype selects the technology and therefore the sign of the reactive contribution; OpenDSS emits a Capacitor for a positive rating and a Reactor for a negative one. A shunt whose technology or rating the source did not disclose is blocked rather than defaulted.

ElmTr3.note: Three-winding transformer. The source star-equivalent (TypTr3 uktr3_h/m/l, each on its own winding rating) is carried verbatim; per-pair impedances are derived for engines that need them.

TypTr3.note: Three-winding transformer type; its per-winding ratings, star-equivalent short-circuit voltages, connections, clocks and tap steps are read into the three-winding row.

TypTow.note: Geometric overhead line type. Its computed conductor matrices R_c/X_c/C_c are read into the line matrix; the tower geometry itself is not reproduced.

TypCabsys.note: Cable system type; carries the conductor matrices for the whole system.

ElmCabsys.note: Cable system: its first circuit becomes the composite branch and the remaining conductors are eliminated into the matrix.

ElmPvsys.note: PV-system element captured as a static-generator row in the typed Case (load-flow representation); the PV/DER + OpenDER co-sim representation boundary is a separate reviewed layer (T-011 follow-on).

ElmVsc.note: Bipolar PWM converter (T-038; following/forming per proven i_acdc map).

ElmDcu.note: Voltage-holding DC (battery) unit with positive uset (T-038).

conditional_note: Some classes only matter when a solver option makes them matter. Those are dispositioned against captured evidence rather than by name: the condition names the exact inventory field it reads, so an 'inert' verdict is checkable and flips automatically when the source says otherwise.

load_flow.inert_reason: PowerFactory balances active power at the slack machine (ComLdf.iopt_apdist=0) and the source designates that reference independently of the controller, so the secondary controller does not change the dispatch this load flow settles on
load_flow.active_reason: the secondary controller is load-bearing for this source: either ComLdf distributes active power by area control (iopt_apdist != 0), or no external grid and no ip_ctrl=1 machine designates a reference, which means the controller itself supplies it. Measured on RBTS Bus 2: 11 machines, all bustp=PV with ip_ctrl=0, no external grid.

dynamics.active_reason: secondary frequency control acts during an RMS simulation; the typed Case has no representation for it

dynamics_rms.active_reason: secondary frequency control acts during an RMS simulation; the typed Case has no representation for it

load_flow.inert_reason: every ElmVac in this source is an ideal ground (usetp=0) and every shield bond is zero impedance, which is exactly the condition the conductor elimination assumes; the earth reference is therefore already represented by folding the neutral/shield into the phase matrix
load_flow.active_reason: an ElmVac holding a non-zero voltage, or a shield bonded through a finite impedance, is a circuit element the phase-domain matrix does not represent
